correctness.rationale: The stationary Gaussian convolution and beta normalization follow from an independent stable linear decomposition. Differentiating the Kummer equation for G=√z F yields zG''+(z+q−1/2)G'+(1−q)G/(2z)=0. For 0<q<1 every G'=0 has G''<0; positive-small-z and negative-large-z derivative signs imply a unique simple crossing. The curvature residual H=2zE[T]−1 satisfies H_z>0 at its unique root and H_q=2zCov(T,log(1−T))<0, proving the exact derivative and sign. Heat evolution ∂δp=p''/2 yields fourth derivative negative at the crossing and the √3 mode-merger coefficient by analytic Taylor expansion. The supplied check.py independently tests critical curvature, negative fourth derivative, square-root attachment, and covariance sensitivity using hypergeometric, Gauss–Jacobi and endpoint-adapted quadratures; numerical evidence is corroboration, not universal proof.

value.rationale: For a physically motivated persistence-versus-thermal-noise phase boundary, the result quantitatively proves how increasing tumbling rate lowers the diffusion budget needed to eliminate two spatial density peaks. Its exact susceptibility and universal local merger law make the critical curve perturbatively predictive, rather than only a numerical diagram, and rule out higher-order flat critical contacts for all interior switching rates. These structural, model-specific critical-response conclusions are not mere normalization tests or arbitrary parameter samples.
